topomer.note: only 8 of 20 molecules can be cut at the framework

descriptors.note: 9 descriptors; dropped as the activity under another name: mwila_hcl_adj, mwila_pooled_raw; not usable as a baseline (see the warning)

findings.text: 9 chemotype(s); the largest holds 7 of 20 molecules -- a series of several scaffolds has no common frame, and an alignment will invent one
the common framework (framework of the largest chemotype) has 17 heavy atoms, about 94% of a typical molecule, and 40% of the set can be cut at it
the 17 shared framework atoms sit 2.4 A apart between molecules, over the best of their matches (8 of 20 carry them) -- the molecules are not in a common frame

the descriptor baseline reproduces the activity almost exactly (q2 +0.992); on a set this size that is not chemistry but the measurement itself, reached through the file's own columns -- the nearest are mwila_pooled_adj (r 0.95), calc:clogp (r 0.69), mw (r 0.57), calc:mw (r 0.57). No descriptor conclusion can be drawn until they are excluded.

dropped from the descriptor baseline because they reproduce the activity rather than describe the molecule: mwila_hcl_adj, mwila_pooled_raw -- if one of these is a real descriptor, name it and run again
the aligned model is -0.059 in q2 against counts (95% interval -0.380 to +0.183) -- the frame buys nothing over counts
the aligned model is -0.447 in q2 against invariant (95% interval -0.883 to -0.029) -- the frame buys nothing over invariant
the aligned model is -1.064 in q2 against descriptors (95% interval -1.556 to -0.925) -- descriptors alone do as well, so the geometry is decoration on this set

why: the frame buys nothing over invariant, which needs no alignment to curate and cannot be got wrong
